newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hardie eyes 5th U.S. cement plant.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hardie eyes 5th U.S. cement plant.

text.p: Building materials supplier James Hardie Industries Ltd said on Wednesday it was looking to purchase land in the northeast of the United States in order to build a fifth fibre cement plant.
James Hardie's president USA, Peter Macdonald, told a briefing that the plant would be open at the earliest in 1998, but could not say what size the plant would be or construction costs.
Macdonald told reporters after the briefing that the company had a couple of site options including locations in Ohio, south of Toronto in Canada, and western Pennsylvania.
"If we press the go button today we would be up... (in) 24 to 36 months," Macdonald said.
He said the planned fifth plant would lift the company's fibre cement production capacity well over the 920 million square feet that is currently planned.
James Hardie currently has plants either operating or under construction in Florida, Texas, California and in the state of Washington.
Shares in James Hardie, which is 27.23 percent owned by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, closed one cent lower at A$3.44.
